# Ecology & Society

> An open-access, peer-reviewed journal publishing transdisciplinary research on the dynamics between social and ecological systems, resilience, and sustainability.

Ecology & Society is a leading publication for scholars studying coupled human-natural systems, with a focus on understanding resilience, adaptive management, and solutions to environmental challenges. The journal emphasizes open-access publishing and welcomes diverse methodological approaches to understanding socio-environmental dynamics.

## Key Topics

- Social-ecological systems
- Resilience
- Sustainability science
- Socio-environmental dynamics
- Fisheries conflict
- Marine ecosystems
- Blame attribution
- Change and stability
- Capture fisheries
- Conflict analysis
- Peatland conservation
- Climate adaptation
- Food systems
- Creative Commons licensing
- Peer review

## Journal Core

- [Home - Ecology & Society](https://ecologyandsociety.org): Journal homepage featuring open-access research on resilience and sustainability
- [Current Issue: Volume 31, Issue 1](https://ecologyandsociety.org/vol31/iss1): Current journal issue with peer-reviewed articles on climate adaptation and food systems
- [Issues Archive](https://ecologyandsociety.org/issue): Archive index of all journal volumes and past publication issues
- [Featured Research](https://ecologyandsociety.org/feature): Special features on water governance and landscape restoration research topics

## Published Articles

- [From Aristotle to Heraclitus: Socio-Environmental Dynamics and Systems Thinking](https://ecologyandsociety.org/vol31/iss1/art37): Peer-reviewed article on socio-environmental dynamics and systems thinking by Sander E. van der Leeuw
- [How Fishers Attribute Blame for Marine Ecosystem Degradation](https://ecologyandsociety.org/vol31/iss1/art36): Peer-reviewed article on fisheries conflict and blame attribution in Croatia
